decisions.quote: The original model results were unavailable as raw data, presented mainly graphically, averaged over 100 simulation runs, and subject to stochastic influences. Using the DOE principles suggested by Lorscheid et al. ( 2012 ), we quantified statistical errors to determine 5,000 simulation runs as an appropriate number enabling reliable visual comparison of graphically depicted outputs. The results of the replicated model generated on this basis match those highlighted by Miller et al. ( 2012 ).
decisions.reason: The codebook defines replication by new data or a different sample, not exclusively human or empirical data. Here, the original raw data were unavailable and the original MATLAB code was not re-run to reproduce reported numbers; instead, the authors translated the published conceptual description into an ODD specification without consulting the original code, implemented a new model in NetLogo, and generated fresh stochastic Monte Carlo simulation samples (100 and 5,000 runs per experiment plus 1,215,000 factorial DOE runs) to compare against the published graphs. Examining the original MATLAB code occurred only after completing the replication (Note 18) as a post-hoc diagnostic check of conceptual alignment, making the focal study a replication.

decisions.quote: The replicated model produces quantitatively similar and qualitatively identical results. According to the classification of Axelrod ( 1997 ), the results are “relationally equivalent” and hint overall at “distributional equivalence” once error variance is taken into account. Hence, we conclude the model is replicated successfully.
decisions.location: Using DOE Principles to Evaluate the Replicated Model
decisions.reason: Because the study is a replication that generates new stochastic simulation data from an independent NetLogo implementation rather than re-analysing the original study's data or re-running its MATLAB code, the scalar replication outcome vocabulary applies. Across Experiments 1–7, the fresh 100-run and 5,000-run simulations yielded qualitatively identical and distributionally equivalent results once Monte Carlo error variance was accounted for, and the authors state an explicit overall verdict that the model was replicated successfully.

prior_decisions.quote: The replication re-implements the conceptual model in a different software and hardware environment to ensure that neither hardware nor software specifics drive results ( Miodownik et al. 2010 ; Wilensky & Rand 2007 ).
prior_decisions.reason: Rather than collecting new empirical data in a different sample, the study re-implements and verifies the computational simulation model of Miller et al. (2012) in NetLogo and screens the original MATLAB code, which is a reproduction under the codebook.

scope_review.parent_objection: The first review labels reproduction partly because no new EMPIRICAL data were collected. The codebook says new data/different sample, not exclusively empirical data. This study independently implements the conceptual model in NetLogo, runs fresh stochastic/MonteCarlo realizations and also screens the original MATLAB code after discrepancies. Determine whether its focal check primarily generates new simulated observations or re-analyses the original study own data/code. Original-code inspection can be substantive reproduction or merely a diagnostic aid; resolve from actual workflow and scope, not field terminology or absence of human data. Settle both type and the applicable outcome vocabulary; do not assume either parent or prior review right.
